clue.text: Bright? Try Latin study

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether taking up Latin would make them clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright?' looks like a remark about the student, but it is the definition, in the sense of gleaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden can describe something shining and brilliant, as a golden sunset; the question mark flags the looser sense.

clue.text: Cheer as doctor in NHS impregnates girl

indicators.note: to impregnate is to fill from within, so one piece goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical scandal: an NHS doctor has fathered a child, an odd thing to call cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun in the NHS story but is a verb meaning tamper with, rearranging IN NHS to NSHIN. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunshine is used figuratively for warmth and happiness, the brightness that lifts the spirits, which is what cheer means.

clue.text: Beers to sell on board?

indicators.note: on board means aboard ship, so the sales word sits inside the ship's letters

parts.note: a steamship is SS, and to be on board is to be on a ship
to tout is to sell, especially pushily

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these beers are what a ship's bar sells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' reads as one idea but splits: board is a ship, and on signals going aboard it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a dark, strong beer brewed with roasted malt, so stouts are kinds of beer.

clue.text: Nuclear researchers keep time with artificial intelligence, for sure

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the research body holds the other letters

parts.note: CERN is the European organisation for nuclear research in Geneva

explanation.surface: Physicists at a big lab are definitely using AI to keep their timing accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is for sure is beyond doubt, which is what certain means.

clue.text: Grasp back muscle during performance

indicators.note: during places one piece within the time, and so the letters, of another

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

indicators.note: back means the muscle's letters run in the reverse direction

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A dancer or acrobat grabs at a strained back muscle mid-show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back muscle' suggests a muscle of the back, but 'back' is the reversal signal, turning the muscle round to CEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to take it in and understand it; to accept it is to receive it as true.

clue.text: Perhaps Eden Hazard's foot is within shot range

indicators.note: within puts the foot letter inside the jumbled letters
shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of range are jumbled
the foot of a word is its last letter, the bottom of it in a down entry

explanation.surface: Eden Hazard, the Belgian footballer, has the ball at his foot and is within shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: GAREN (an anagram of RANGE, signalled by 'shot') takes D, the last letter of Hazard, inside it. Eden Hazard played for Chelsea, so the surface is about football.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the Bible's paradise, an example of a garden, hence the Perhaps.

clue.text: Offer to tour elven ruins

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters of these words are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: An invitation to go sightseeing round some ruins built by elves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' looks like a noun, the place to tour, but it is the verb signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to offer oneself or one's services freely, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Canoe might capsize here?

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns over, so the letters of canoe are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking where a small boat is likely to overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Open sea, with its large waves, is a place where a small paddled boat could easily turn over.

clue.text: At twilight in EU, Norway thanks Finland's parliament

indicators.note: in places the evening word inside the two letters of EU

parts.note: twilight is dusk
N is the international vehicle code for Norway
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: As the sun sets at a European meeting, Norway thanks the Finnish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface is wordplay apart from the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eduskunta is the name of the single-chamber Finnish legislature in Helsinki.

clue.text: Prepare bread

definitions.meaning: to prepare something is to get it set to use
bread is slang for money, and ... money is cash, the readies

explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' looks like the thing to prepare but is slang for money, which is also the readies in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready something is to prepare it, and ready (as in ready money) is slang for cash, like bread.

clue.text: Opposed to local migrant integration

indicators.note: local means found in a particular place, so the letters are found sitting within these words

explanation.surface: Someone is against efforts to help migrants become part of a local community.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition anti means against, the same as opposed to.

clue.text: When outside, they're never homeless

parts.note: these garden creatures carry their shells with them, so wherever they go outdoors their house goes too

explanation.surface: It reads like a remark about rough sleepers, which turns out to be about garden molluscs.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden molluscs carry their shell as a portable house, so they are never without a home.

clue.text: Flaming double gin mixed with vermouth

indicators.note: the letters are mixed like a cocktail
a double gin is two measures, so the word is taken twice

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A bartender makes a flaming cocktail from a double gin and vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double gin' gives GINGIN, and 'with vermouth' adds IT (Italian vermouth, as in the old cocktail gin and It); 'mixed' shuffles all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Igniting is catching fire or setting on fire, so something igniting is in flames.

clue.text: Travel north or south in Winnipeg to find hotel

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading the letters upwards, and here either direction works
in means the letters sit inside the city name

explanation.surface: Directions to finding a hotel in the Canadian city of Winnipeg.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or pub offering rooms for travellers.

clue.text: For example, over 1,000 stone

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Weighing something at more than a thousand stone, the old British unit of fourteen pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' looks like the unit of weight, but it is the definition, a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem is a precious or semi-precious stone cut for jewellery.

clue.text: Inner nature throughout Asian city (not just including capitals)

parts.note: in can mean throughout a period, as in in the winter

indicators.note: not means the capital letters are left out of the city

parts.note: Beijing is the capital of China

indicators.note: the capitals of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A geography note about a city that is more than merely a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just including capitals' is read literally: the initial letters of just and including, J and I, are removed from BEIJING.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbeing is a rare philosophical word for essence, the inherent existence or nature within a thing.

clue.text: Type of drink with cap removed

indicators.note: a bottle's cap is its top, so the first letter is taken away

parts.note: milk is a drink

explanation.surface: Describing a kind of drink whose bottle top has been taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or sort, as in people of that ilk, so it matches type.

clue.text: Always chasing black horse

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the black letter

parts.note: B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
ay or aye is an old word for always, as in for ay

explanation.surface: A black horse is forever in pursuit, perhaps in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat and black mane and tail.

clue.text: Ohio doubly in the news at 12

indicators.note: in puts the doubled letter inside the other pair

parts.note: news read as the plural of new, N's: N, the abbreviation for new, twice

indicators.note: doubly means the letter is taken twice

parts.note: O is an old abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: A headline about Ohio featuring twice in the midday news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at 12' sounds like a broadcast time; 12 alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, so the number stands for that hour.

clue.text: Country against having it's name changed hasn't succeeded

parts.note: v is short for versus, against

indicators.note: changed means the remaining letters are rearranged
hasn't means the letter for succeeded is missing

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A nation that tried to rename itself but failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't succeeded' removes S from IT'S NAME; 'changed' turns ITNAME into IETNAM, after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Tears flow on getting flower as prize

indicators.note: tears flowing are running freely, so these letters run into a new order

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Someone weeps with joy at being handed a bouquet as their prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword trick: a thing that flows, here the River Ure in Yorkshire, England. 'flow' rearranges TEARS into TREAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to prize it, value it highly; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Extremely blonde, what I have is a 1960s' hairstyle

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, the first and last, of blonde

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A very blonde woman shows off her retro bouffant.
explanation.definitionFit: The beehive was a tall rounded bouffant style fashionable for women in the 1960s.

clue.text: It's essential to follow clues by directions

indicators.note: follow places the word to after the clues word

parts.note: keys are clues that unlock answers
N and E are compass directions, north and east

explanation.surface: A treasure-hunt rule: you must follow the clues to find your way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' looks like an instruction to the solver, but it only orders the pieces; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central stone locking an arch, and figuratively the vital part on which everything depends.

clue.text: European politician's anger with group of states …

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A European politician fumes at a bloc of countries.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a set of nations or territories ruled by a single power.

clue.text: … preferably in case one's heading for referendum

parts.note: so can mean in order that, the sense of in case
one is taken as written, with the 's read as has

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone wants the group of states to hold a vote, ideally soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sooner is used to mean rather, as in I'd sooner walk, expressing a preference.

clue.text: Unwilling to serve out after ace

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled serve after the ace letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A tennis player, having served an ace, does not want to serve again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve' and 'ace' both suggest tennis, but ace is the card letter A and 'out' rearranges SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be averse to something is to be opposed to it or reluctant, much the same as unwilling.

clue.text: Temptation of a solution when 100 is divided by 2?

indicators.note: a hundred divided into two halves is fifty and fifty, the Roman L twice, which takes the place of the hundred

parts.note: a cure is a solution to a problem
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle asks why a solution might be tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman hundred is split into two halves of fifty, each written L, so one C becomes LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractive power or charm, the pull that tempts someone.

clue.text: Metal, a thin piece with lithium twisted inside

indicators.note: the symbol for lithium inside the thin piece is turned round where it sits

parts.note: a sliver is a thin piece
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A metallurgist describes a thin strip of metal with lithium worked into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Ghost upset king — I'm so sorry!

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
oops! is the apology for a blunder

explanation.surface: A ghost has frightened a king and apologises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the king's state but reverses K OOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is an informal word for a ghost or spirit.

clue.text: Pit in Wales demolished completely

indicators.note: in places the pit inside the rearranged country
demolished means knocked down, so the letters of Wales are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: a pit is a hole

explanation.surface: A coal mine in Wales is entirely torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests a Welsh coal mine but is just a hole; 'demolished' rearranges the country into WSALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale used as an adverb means on a large scale, indiscriminately, so entirely.

clue.text: Short, strong cheese as starter

indicators.note: the cheese course comes first here, before the loud letter

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
F is forte, loud or strong in music

explanation.surface: A diner chooses a strong cheese to start a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means lasting a short time, so it is a synonym for short.

clue.text: Cluedo character goes topless endlessly, like Holly?

indicators.note: read literally, without the word end, so those three letters drop out
the top of the character's name, its first letter, is removed

parts.note: Reverend Green is a suspect in Cluedo, the British murder-mystery board game sold as Clue in the US

explanation.surface: A Cluedo suspect strips off endlessly, like a character in a soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' is literal: END is taken out of EVEREND GREEN. 'Holly' looks like a name but is the plant, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly keeps its leaves through winter, so it is an example of a plant that stays green all year.
